Though there is no observation that cross-examination of PW-2 and PW-3 was deferred but right to cross-examination was never closed.
However, if for arguments, testimony of PW-2 and PW-3 is considered to be un-rebutted, it neeeds to evaluated independently.

perusal of evidentiary affidavit of PW-2 and PW- 3 Durgesh shows that they stated that they reached at spot on hue and cry of some passers by and found that a motor cycle struck with the electric pole which was installed in the centre of road and police was called.
Even if evidence is taken on face value, admittedly PW-2 and PW-3 have not seen as to how plaintiff struck electric pole in question.
Therefore, whether there was any negligence of plaintiff, it cannot be assessed from testimony of PW-2 and PW-3.
Hence, testimony of PW-2 and PW-3 are not of much consequence.
Though PW-2 and PW-3 stated that electric pole was in middle of road, however, except this assertion, no other material is placed on record to support this assertion.
